stages.name: Password Spraying and Brute Force
observables: Single common password tested against many accounts
Iterative password guessing against a single account
Spikes in authentication failures (activity_id 5)
Logins from unfamiliar IP addresses or geographic locations

stages.name: Credential Stuffing
observables: Authentication attempts using username/password pairs leaked in previous third-party breaches
High volume of failed login attempts across diverse accounts

stages.name: Infostealer Data Collection
observables: Access to browser profile directories (e.g., AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data)
Reading of 'Cookies' and 'Login Data' SQLite databases
Exfiltration of harvested credentials to external C2 nodes
Processes running from Temp or Downloads directories

stages.name: LSASS Credential Dumping
observables: procdump -ma lsass.exe
rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll MiniDump
Execution of Mimikatz or similar tools
Creation of .dmp files containing LSASS memory

stages.name: Registry Hive Extraction
observables: reg.exe save HKLM\SAM
reg.exe save HKLM\SYSTEM
reg.exe save HKLM\SECURITY
esentutl.exe /y /vss /d
Access to %SystemRoot%\System32\config

stages.name: Valid Account Abuse and Impossible Travel
observables: Impossible travel (logins from distant locations in rapid succession)
Logins that bypass MFA using stolen session tokens
Unauthorized privilege changes or administrative role assignments
MFA enrollments for new/unrecognized devices

scenario.summary: This campaign involves the unauthorized acquisition of credentials via phishing, brute force, and infostealers to impersonate legitimate users. Attackers then perform credential dumping on compromised endpoints to harvest cached passwords and hashes, enabling lateral movement and full account takeover.

meta.rationale: Focus on high-value identity infrastructure such as domain controllers, AD FS servers, and cloud identity proxies. Widen the lookback to 30 days if slow-and-low spraying is suspected.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder is testing passwords against identity providers to gain initial access or using stolen session tokens to bypass MFA and access internal resources.

scope_hosts.description: List of hostnames identified in the scoping step to focus the authentication analysis.

lookback_days.description: Days of history to examine for authentication patterns.

suspicious_ips.description: Known-malicious or suspicious IPs from external intelligence to prioritize.

spray_threshold.description: Minimum number of unique accounts targeted by a single source IP to qualify as spraying.

references.name: Huntress — Credential Theft: How Attackers Steal & Use Stolen Credentials

blind_spots.risk: A successful takeover of a standalone SaaS account using stolen credentials would be invisible.
blind_spots.question: whether the attacker successfully logged into an application not covered by the current log ingestion
blind_spots.requires: Unified logging (hb_auth_signin) for all critical SaaS and cloud providers.
blind_spots.remediation: Integrate all business-critical SaaS platforms into the centralized identity provider or SIEM.

blind_spots.risk: The hunt may misinterpret session reuse as a legitimate return visit if auth_protocol metadata is missing.
blind_spots.question: whether a successful logon used a password or a stolen session cookie
blind_spots.requires: Authentication logs that distinguish between password-based and token-based logins.
blind_spots.remediation: Enable advanced identity logging to capture session token usage details.

hunt.name: Identity Authentication and Account Abuse
hunt.description: This hunt examines the authentication plane for signs of high-volume credential testing and subsequent account takeover. It starts by identifying hosts running identity-related software or browsers to scope the estate, then analyzes authentication failures for spraying patterns and successful logons for anomalous behavior, such as multiple source IPs per user or access to sensitive systems. An agent triages the combined evidence to distinguish legitimate remote access from active compromise.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname, package_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%active directory%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%chrome%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%firefox%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%edge%'
config.description: Locate hosts running Active Directory components, domain services, or common browsers where credentials may be dumped or used.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames. These are the assets where credential-based lateral movement is most impactful. Use these to fill the scope_hosts parameter.

primitive_config.label: Identify identity-sensitive assets
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname, package_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%active directory%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%chrome%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%firefox%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%edge%'
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames. These are the assets where credential-based lateral movement is most impactful. Use these to fill the scope_hosts parameter.

config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) AS unique_accounts, COUNT(*) AS total_failures, MIN(time) AS first_seen, MAX(time) AS last_seen FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 2 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{suspicious_ips}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{suspicious_ips}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip HAVING unique_accounts >= {{spray_threshold}}
config.description: Identify source IPs that target a high volume of accounts with failed authentication attempts.
config.expected_signal: Source IPs hitting many unique usernames. A high unique_account count suggests spraying; high failure counts against a single user suggest brute force.

primitive_config.label: Detect credential spraying and stuffing
primitive_config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) AS unique_accounts, COUNT(*) AS total_failures, MIN(time) AS first_seen, MAX(time) AS last_seen FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 2 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{suspicious_ips}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{suspicious_ips}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip HAVING unique_accounts >= {{spray_threshold}}
primitive_config.expected: Source IPs hitting many unique usernames. A high unique_account count suggests spraying; high failure counts against a single user suggest brute force.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_name, COUNT(*) AS login_count, MIN(time) AS first_login FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_name || ',') > 0) GROUP BY actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_name ORDER BY login_count DESC
config.description: Find successful logons that deviate from normal patterns, particularly targeting assets identified in scoping.
config.expected_signal: Successful logons to sensitive hosts or users with high source IP diversity. Cross-referencing these source IPs with the spraying results reveals account takeover.

primitive_config.label: Detect anomalous successful logons
primitive_config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_name, COUNT(*) AS login_count, MIN(time) AS first_login FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_name || ',') > 0) GROUP BY actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_name ORDER BY login_count DESC
primitive_config.expected: Successful logons to sensitive hosts or users with high source IP diversity. Cross-referencing these source IPs with the spraying results reveals account takeover.

config.objective: Determine if any successful logons were preceded by spraying from the same IP, or if users exhibit impossible travel or access to sensitive scoped hosts from suspicious origins.
config.description: Correlate failed authentication leads with successful logon anomalies to confirm account compromise.
config.expected_signal: A per-user and per-IP verdict citing rows from both spraying and success queries.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious | suspicious | benign for each identified actor, citing specific rows.

config.question: the triage-identity-abuse verdict is malicious for at least one user
config.condition: the triage-identity-abuse verdict is malicious for at least one user
config.description: Direct the workflow to containment if a compromise is confirmed.
Revoke attacker access immediately to prevent further lateral movement.
config.instructions: Suspend the identified user account in the identity provider and revoke all active session tokens to invalidate any stolen cookies.

config.description: Perform an analyst check of the findings and look for post-compromise activity.
config.instructions: Review the successful logons for malicious users. Examine process and file activity on the targeted hosts (scope_hosts) originating from those users to identify lateral movement or data staging.

config.description: Finalize the hunt and address structural identity risks.
config.instructions: Document the findings and IPs. Identify any accounts that successfully authenticated without MFA and coordinate with the identity team to enforce phishing-resistant MFA controls.
